overview_markdown:
Picobot is a minimalist, Go-based reimplementation of the OpenClaw personal AI agent concept, packaged as a single ~9MB static binary with zero runtime dependencies. It delivers the core agent loop — persistent memory, tool calling, skills, and multi-channel messaging (Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp) — while idling at roughly 10MB of RAM and booting in milliseconds, making it viable on a $5 VPS, Raspberry Pi, or even an Android phone via Termux.

Configuration is handled through environment variables and a simple `onboard` CLI flow, with all state persisted to a single data directory that maps cleanly into Docker volumes. Recent development shows active maintenance: a configurable exec-command denylist for safer shell tool use, a configurable agent timeout (raised from a hardcoded 60s to 300s) applied consistently across CLI and gateway channels, improved Slack socket-mode error logging, and growing test coverage.

Compared to OpenClaw, Picobot deliberately sacrifices breadth — no control UI, no canvas, a much smaller skills ecosystem, and fewer integrations — in exchange for operational simplicity and an extremely small resource footprint. It is best understood as the 'runs anywhere' end of the OpenClaw-alternative spectrum: ideal for solo self-hosters who want a private, always-on chat agent without managing Python environments or heavyweight containers.
